speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and do you notice any pain specifically when you urinate?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since your symptoms are relieved by voiding and you report recent dyspareunia (painful intercourse), I want to rule out a lower urinary tract issue or pelvic floor dysfunction. Have you noticed any blood in your urine, fever, or flank pain recently? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis (Painful Bladder Syndrome)

Your symptoms of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, frequency, urgency, and dyspareunia, combined with the absence of fever, hematuria, or infection in your urinalysis, are not consistent with a Urinary Tract Infection. These findings are classic for Interstitial Cystitis.
